question.problem: Find a basis of the null space of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
To find a basis of $\text{Null}(A),$ we need to solve the equation $Ax=0$ and express the solution as a linear combination of linearly independent vectors. Those vectors form a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$

The given matrix is already in row echelon form. So, the equation $Ax=0$ corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}+2{x}_{4}=0 \\ {x}_{4}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{4}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Here, ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{3}$, and ${x}_{4}$ are basic variables corresponding to the pivot columns ($1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th) and ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable corresponding to the non-pivot column. Therefore, if $x\in \text{Null}(A),$ then

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${x}_{2}\in R.$ This implies that

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}
$$

is a basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate the $\text{Null}(A).$
